title: What Is the World to Me?
description: What Is the World to Me? in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Georg Michael Pfefferkorn, first published in 1667. The English translation is by August Crull (1893). The tune, WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT, is by Ahasverus Fritsch (1679). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: What is the world to me With all its vaun-ted plea_-sure When Thou, and Thou a-lone, Lord Je-sus, art my Trea_-sure! Thou o-nly, dea-rest Lord, My soul's De-light shalt be; Thou art my Peace, my Rest, What is the world to me!

lines: What is the world to me
Thou art my Peace, my Rest,
What is the world to me!
The world is like a cloud
Though all things fade and flee;
What is the world to me!
The world seeks to be praised
That they are frail and flighty.
What is the world to me!
Though gold should fill its coffers.
What is the world to me!
What is the world to me!
